subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm designing a futuristic 6-wheel armored military truck with a cab, cargo bed turret/missile launcher, neon glow accents, and SVG-based textures like camo panels, decals, and emblems, keeping the structure simple with optional joints for wheels and the turret.

Setting up the chassis joint, wheel axle positions and dimensions, and a helper function to build box parts, then designing the wheel assembly with tires, rims, and glowing hub rings...

Working out the cab geometry using an extruded profile for the sloped windshield and hood, designing the side outline with points that taper up toward the front for an armored wedge look.

Still building body geometry...

Working out the cab side window geometry so it fits the sloped front edge, then placing dark thin door line boxes. For the rear cargo bed I'm sizing a paneled hull box and planning a missile launcher pod rack on the roof.

Now I'm designing the turret: a rotating ring joint on the bed holding a twin railgun housing with sweeping barrels and glowing cyan coil rings, plus cab-roof missile pods, an antenna array, roof lightbar, front plow bumper, glowing headlights, neon underglow strips, side skirts, cargo crates, exhaust stacks, chevron-striped armor plates, a sensor dome, door emblem decals, "2077" numbering, rear ramp lights, and a spinning LIDAR dome -- aiming for 6-8 distinct textures overall, starting with the glass windshield.

Beyond that I'm planning more textures: HUD side windows, a star-shield door emblem, hazard stripes, mottled camo paint patches, a glowing headlight beam plane, a stenciled "UNIT 77-ZX" license plate, ammo crate labels, a radar screen with sweep glow, and a hex-grid armor vent mesh. For the hull paint I'm building a dark-olive mottled patch pattern, keeping the color palette under the 64-flat-color limit, then setting up builder helper functions for joints and boxes to construct the chassis.

Writing box and cylinder helper functions...

I'm importing the glow effect from the kits module to wrap flat-colored parts, adding thin cyan underglow boxes beneath the skirts, and now laying out the concrete world-space coordinates for each part attached to the main chassis bone, separating out the wheels as their own joints.

I'm checking that the hull doesn't clip into the wheels given their radius and position, so I'm raising the hull's bottom edge and adding fender boxes above each wheel to cover the arch.

Now I'm working out the cab's cross-section coordinates, including a sloped windshield, and figuring out the normal vector for that angled surface.

Still placing geometry details...

Adjusting grille width and headlight placement, then shaping the front bumper and plow using extruded wedge profiles...

Now I'm planning the roof details: a sensor dome, light bar, antennas, and missile pods mounted on either side of the cab roof, tilted upward with glowing cylindrical tube ends.

Working out tube rotation math...

Now I'm planning the turret assembly — a joint at the chassis top with a ring base, a box housing, and a child gun joint with hinge pitch for the barrels.

Twin barrels extend forward as rods from the gun position, spaced apart in x, with ring-shaped coil segments along their length for a glowing cyan effect, plus a muzzle brake box at the tip. I'm checking the geometry so the barrels clear the cab roof height and extend out past the turret front without clipping.

I'm raising the turret mount height so the barrels sit above the cab roof with clearance, then adjusting the bed hull dimensions and shape to taper slightly at the back with beveled, panelled armor plating, placing the turret ring on top. Overall vehicle height comes to roughly 4.1 meters including antennas, which fits a large military design.

Now I'm adding side details to the bed: hazard stripe and armor chevron textures on side panels, door emblems, ammo boxes and cargo racks mounted on the flanks, plus rooftop details like hex vents, a radar dish on a mast, and fuel tank cylinders between the axles.

Reconsidering tank placement since the radius would collide with the chassis frame, I decide to skip underslung tanks and instead add vertical exhaust stacks behind the cab, positioned outside the hull width with glowing hot tips, along with heat shield boxes and glowing red tail lights at the rear.

Now I'm working through the suspension system: axle rods spanning the chassis width at each wheel position, a differential housing sphere at center, plus leaf spring boxes and shock cylinders, with a drive shaft connecting everything.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Still writing tread geometry...

For the hub, I'm designing an SVG with a dark circle, six silver spokes, and a cyan center ring for the star emblem. I'm also placing neon underglow boxes along the chassis edges for the cyan lighting effect, checking that wheel contact points stay at floor level, and sketching an emblem SVG combining a shield, star, and "77" text.

Now I'm detailing more SVG textures: a hexagonal shield emblem with cyan outline and "2077" text, hazard warning stripes using diagonal yellow/black patterns, and a radar-style tactical display plane for the truck bed with glowing green blips. I'm also setting up the camo hull paint using mottled olive tones layered with paneling and rivets, then adding magenta/cyan cyber accent highlights over a darker iron metallic base.

Writing camo paint function...

Adding roof details: a rear armor box, an alternating cyan/red lightbar near the windshield top, a sensor dome built from a sphere and cylinder base, a spinning sensor head box with a glowing cyan slit, and rod-shaped antennas mounted on the roof.

Now I'm positioning missile pods on the cab roof with tilted boxes and support structures, checking clearances against the dome and gun barrels so nothing overlaps near the front.

Let me move the mast to the cab roof at x=0.9 instead, keeping pods narrower so they clear the cab width, and relocate the lidar to the rear bed center behind the turret where the gun barrels won't sweep through it. I'm checking the turret housing and barrel spans against the lidar's position to confirm clearance, then considering a small sensor cluster below the barrels as an alternative to a roof-mounted unit.

Now I'm thinking through the remaining greebling details to add—fenders, mirrors, lights, exhaust, racks, decals, and other small parts—aiming for roughly 200 total pieces, and planning to write the code with loops over left/right symmetry to keep things efficient. I'm also starting to define texture assets, like an SVG-based glass material with a gradient and reflection polygons for the canopy.

Writing texture SVGs...

Writing truck builder setup...

Still writing extrusion and wheel joint setup...

Still positioning tread blocks...

Still positioning fender lips and mud flaps...

I'm adding a glow strip underneath near the frame edge, then working out side skirt panels between the wheel positions, checking the clearance gaps based on axle spacing to make sure the skirts don't overlap the tires.

Checking the skirt placement stays clear of the tires and adding a hazard texture strip on its outer face, painted in dark metal. Now I'm planning the cab details—door outlines and seams rendered as thin dark boxes on either side of the cab.

Still working out door armor plate geometry and emblem placement coordinates...

Now I'm adding cab hull paint panels, windshield wipers, and side mirrors — sketching the mirror arm as a rod connecting to a small dark-glass box angled outward from the window frame.

Next I'm placing the roof plate and vents, then adding rear exhaust stacks to the cab back. For the bed, I'm positioning side racks, ammo crates, and a turret base, spacing crates along the sides near the lidar mount and sketching a tactical screen decal for the bed's side panel.

Now I'm detailing bed sides with an emblem plane on the left, a radar screen texture on the right, hazard stripe bands, hex vents, and armor rib boxes spaced along the length. For the rear, I'm adding a back plate, lights, a ramp plane, and a license plate placement.

I'm figuring out the rear slanted hull profile with the bed's extrusion points, then setting up the turret joint parented to the chassis, aimed upward at the correct offset position.

Working out the turret ring, collar, and body box dimensions and vertical placements so the gun mantlet sits correctly above the ring without clipping.

Adding coil rings along the barrel sleeve with a cyan glow and a muzzle brake cap at the barrel tip, then checking overall height clearance so the gun, turret roof, and radar mast all stack correctly without colliding.

For turret detailing, I'm placing small tilted smoke launcher tubes on each side of the turret body with red-glowing tips, then adding a lidar joint on the hull with a stationary base cylinder and a spinning sensor head on top.

Working out the glow ring and cyan light on the lidar head, then positioning a light bar across the top with alternating red and blue glowing boxes, and roughing out side pod supports with their own dimensions and placement.

Now I'm computing the tilted pod boxes, checking the bottom corner geometry so the pod sits flush with its support, then laying out a 2x3 grid of tube centers in local coordinates to be rotated into world space using the pod's tilt angle.

Giving the tubes a dark body with an orange glowing core, then adding forward-pointing hazard spikes along the bumper near the plow nose.

Now I'm placing the plow's wedge geometry with clearance off the ground, adding a hazard-striped front face plane, fog lamps mounted on either side of the plow, and starting on hood vent details along the sloped hood surface.

Still placing grille and headlight elements...

Still writing SVG code...

Finalizing the extrude helper's typing and assembling the complete code now, skipping mirror glass glow for simplicity.
